Who benefits: Recreational boaters seeking enhanced safety compliance and peace of mind.. Why behaviour changes: Regulatory pressure (e.g., maritime safety rules) and media coverage of boating accidents make a certified beacon a required or strongly recommended item, shifting perception from optional luxury to essential safety gear.. How value is captured: ACR can charge premium prices for a certified, differentiated beacon and capture value through direct-to-consumer sales and brand association with safety compliance.. T2: Individual consumers will purchase a 406 MHz distress beacon for recreational boating if they view it as a status symbol or fashion accessory, leading to demand for a differentiated, aesthetically designed product. Test "Recreational vs Everyday Consumer Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online choice-based conjoint survey with willingness-to-pay questions.. Sample: 500 participants: 250 self-identified recreational users (shooting, hunting, outdoor sports) and 250 everyday users (musicians, remote workers, travelers). Decision rule: If recreational users choose the performance model in ≥60% of choices AND their average WTP for it is ≥20% higher than for the everyday model, proceed to develop a differentiated recreational line. If neither condition is met, no expansion.. Cost: 15000 euros, 10 weeks.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether Deere & Company should invest in creating a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case that leverages its tractor engineering, based on evidence available in mid-1962.. Constraints: Limited to public sources published before mid-1962; no internal company data available.; Test budget of €20,000 and 12‑week timeline for any proposed experiment.; Must identify evidence of consumer demand, market size, competitive landscape, and feasibility of adapting tractor technology to a consumer use case.; Must consider Deere’s existing dealer network and its current reach to individual buyers.. Alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case (e.g., small‑farm or hobbyist tractor) using Deere’s engineering.; 2) Expand the existing dealer network to reach more individual buyers without a differentiated proposition (e.g., marketing tractors directly to smallholders).; 3) No expansion: continue focusing on the current farm and industrial equipment market.; 4) License Deere’s tractor technology to third‑party manufacturers for consumer applications.; 5) Create a new brand or sub‑brand targeting a different customer segment (e.g., urban gardeners) while retaining the core farm business..

Test "Consumer vs Commercial Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with randomized messaging exposure. Recruit 400 respondents: 200 households with small gardens (verified by self‑report of garden size <0.5 acre) and 200 professional landscapers/small farm operators (verified by self‑report of commercial use). Randomly assign each respondent to either a consumer‑focused message (emphasizing low cost, ease of use, and suitability for small gardens) or a commercial‑focused message (emphasizing durability, service support, and suitability for professional work). After exposure, ask: "How likely are you to purchase a John Deere garden tractor?" on a 1‑10 scale. Also ask: "What is the maximum price you would pay?" and "Would you recommend this to others in your segment?". The test will be run in 12 weeks with a €20,000 budget for platform fees, incentives, and data analysis.. Sample: 400 respondents (200 small‑garden households, 200 professional landscapers/small farm operators).. Measure: Average purchase intent score (1‑10) for each segment under each message condition.. Predictions: T1: Households with small gardens will show higher purchase intent when exposed to the consumer message than when exposed to the commercial message.; T2: Professional landscapers/small farm operators will show higher purchase intent when exposed to the commercial message than when exposed to the consumer message.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between the two message conditions for households with small gardens is at least 1.5 points (on the 10‑point scale) and the difference for professionals is at least 1.5 points in the opposite direction, then both theories are supported and the test is inconclusive for a single recommendation. If only one segment shows a ≥1.5‑point. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.
